## Your First Action

Call the `descix_doctor` MCP tool immediately. It returns your auth state,
workspace context, available tools, and any configuration issues. Use its
output to orient yourself before doing anything else.

## What is DeSciX?

DeSciX is a platform for building knowledge-powered applications. Think of
it as a virtual university where:

- **Communities** are departments — each has an on-chain identity and members
- **Apps** are anything: courses, textbooks, problem sets, simulations, services
- **Knowledge bases** are the source material — markdown docs vectorized for AI retrieval
- **You (the AI agent)** are the primary interface for building and navigating

Any community member can build apps, contribute knowledge, and use AI tools
to interact with the community's collective knowledge.

## Setup Workflow

If `descix_doctor` reports `setup_needed: true`, guide the user through these
checkpoints. **Ask the user at each step** — don't assume.

### Checkpoint 1: Objective
> "Do you want to explore existing apps, or build something new?"

### Checkpoint 2: Community & App Selection
Use `find_communities` and `list_apps_for_community` to show options, then ask:
> "Which community and app should this project target?"

### Checkpoint 3: Environment
> "Should this run against local dev backend (localhost:4000) or hosted API?"

### Canonical Setup Commands (run in terminal after checkpoints)
```bash
descix whoami                              # confirm identity
descix app list                            # see available apps
descix init -c <community> -a <app> -p .   # create workspace.json
descix app init -a <app> -c <community>    # register app on platform
```

### Checkpoint 4: Content Strategy
> "Should I create a starter KB doc now, or wait for your domain docs?"

### Checkpoint 5: Frontend Scope
> "Do you want plain HTML, or should I set up a framework (React, VitePress, etc.)?"

## Important: Use Explicit Flags

Until workspace context is verified working, **always use explicit flags**
for all CLI commands:
```bash
descix chat -c <community> -a <app> -q "..."
descix update kb -c <community> -a <app>
descix kb sync -c <community> -a <app> --kb General
```

Implicit defaults can silently target the wrong app. After setup, verify
with `descix chat -c <community> -a <app> -q "test"` before dropping flags.

## Success Criteria

After setup, verify all of these pass:
- [ ] App visible in `descix app list`
- [ ] `descix update kb -c <community> -a <app>` succeeds (KB sync)
- [ ] `descix chat -c <community> -a <app> -q "..."` returns response with source attribution

## App Structure

Every app has three parts:
- `site/` — Frontend (any framework: React, VitePress, vanilla HTML)
- `kb/General/` — Knowledge base source docs (markdown files)
- `microservice/` — Backend service (optional)

- App ID: `{{appId}}`

## Available MCP Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `descix_doctor` | Startup diagnostic — call first |
| `ask_question_to_app` | RAG chat with any app's knowledge base |
| `query_knowledge_base` | Raw vector search (returns chunks) |
| `find_communities` | List communities on the platform |
| `list_apps_for_community` | List apps in a community |
| `tell_me_how` | Discover any platform capability by asking |

## Known CLI Quirks

- `descix status` may report "No workspace found" even when `.descix/workspace.json`
  exists. This is a known bug — continue with explicit flags.
- `descix status` may suggest `descix setup` — that command doesn't exist. Use
  `descix init -c <community> -a <app> -p .` instead.
